gloss: in scattered drops; one by one; haltingly

definitions.gloss: in scattered drops; one by one; here and there
definitions.explanation: Describes things falling or appearing singly at intervals — the first drops of rain, people arriving a few at a time, lights dotted across a dark landscape.
Describes speech that comes out slowly in short bursts with pauses between, typically because the speaker is reluctant, tired, or choosing words with care.

examples.japanese: {雨|あめ}がぽつりぽつりと{降|ふ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The rain began to fall in scattered drops.

examples.japanese: {客|きゃく}がぽつりぽつりと{入|はい}ってきた。
examples.english: Customers came in a few at a time.

examples.japanese: {山道|やまみち}を{下|くだ}ると、{谷|たに}の{向|む}こうに{家|いえ}の{明|あ}かりがぽつりぽつりと{見|み}えた。
examples.english: As we came down the mountain road, house lights were dotted here and there across the valley.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}はぽつりぽつりと{話|はな}し{始|はじ}めた。
{母|はは}は{昔|むかし}のことをぽつりぽつりと{語|かた}った。
examples.english: My mother spoke of the past a little at a time.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}い{沈黙|ちんもく}のあと、{彼女|かのじょ}はぽつりぽつりと{当時|とうじ}の{気持|きも}ちを{説明|せつめい}してくれた。
examples.english: After a long silence, she explained how she had felt at the time, a few words at a time.

notes:
A mimetic adverb, almost always used with と. It is a variant of ぽつぽつ built on ぽつり, and carries a slower, more spaced-out feeling: each drop, person, or phrase is separated by a noticeable gap.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ぽつりぽつりと{降|ふ}る: to fall in scattered drops
- ぽつりぽつりと{話|はな}す: to talk haltingly
- ぽつりぽつりと{集|あつ}まる: to gather a few at a time

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ぽつぽつ: bit by bit; in drops — the same range of meaning, but faster and more continuous
- ちらほら: here and there — about scattered numbers only, never about speech
